Latency
following
bradykinin
stimulation

The
activation
of
B2
receptors
by
bradykinin
in
cells
injected
with
FFP - 18
( 1mM

micropipette
concentration )
or
mag - fura - 2
( 1mM )
results
in
a
latent
period
( mean
latency
=
9.06

seconds )
preceding
a
rise
in
intracellular
[ Ca2 + ]
( Fig .
1-2 ) .
[ Ca2 + ] ;
increases
to
approximately

2μM
( an
estimated
20
fold
increase
from
resting
Ca2 +
levels )
within
2-5
seconds
following
initial

response .
The
increase
in
[ Ca2 + ] ;
is
followed
by
a
characteristic
falling
phase
where
fluorescence

exhibits
a
smooth
decay
to
resting
levels .
The
decay
of
mag - fura - 2
appears
more
rapid
than
the

decay
of
FFP - 18 .
The
high
affinity
of
FFP - 18
for
Ca2 +
causes
it
to
reach
saturation
well
before

peak
[ Ca2 + ]
is
attained ,
accounting
for
the
slower
apparent
decay
of
the
signal .

Latency
following
flash
photolysis
of
caged
IP3

Flash
photolysis
of
cells
injected
with
caged
IP3
plus
fluo - 3
( 1mM
micropipette

concentrations )
does
not
exhibit
a
latent
period
prior
to
the
rise
in
intracellular
[ Ca2 + ]
( Fig .
3 ) .

Photolysis
occurs
instantaneously
following
shutter
closure
( see
Materials
and
Methods )
and
is

represented
by
a
decline
in
fluorescence .
Response
to
uncaging
in
the
single
cell ,
illustrated
in
Fig

3. ,
is
characterized
by
an
immediate
rise
( within
200ms )
in
[ Ca2 + ] ,
with
peak
levels
reached
in
less

than
1
second .
Peak
[ Ca2 + ]
corresponds
to
approximately
600nM
( an
estimated
6
fold
increase

from
resting
levels ) .
An
averaged
response
to
flash
photolysis
of
caged
IP3
( Fig .
4 )
shows
similar

results ,
but
exhibits
a
noticeably
slower
rise
to
maximum
Ca2 +
levels
( 2-3
seconds
following

photolysis ) .
The
attainment
of
peak
[ Ca2 + ] ;
is
followed
by
a
falling
phase
where
fluorescence

exhibits
exponential
decay
to
resting
levels
( Fig .
5 ) .
The
time
to
one - half
decay
was
measured
to

be
4.06
seconds .
